title: bug: the VS Code extension reads .moe/daemon.json with no size cap
description:
Objective: bound every .moe/daemon.json read in moe-vscode. Each of these call sites reads the whole file with fs.readFileSync:
- src/services/MoeDaemonClient.ts: the connection lookup (~:604);
- src/services/MoeDaemonClient.ts: the wait-for-daemon loop (~:792), which re-reads the file until a timeout;
- src/extension.ts: the status quick-pick (~:196).
This is a sibling of task-4f1e37f30ee548298b26e17c0b6ea84e (the JetBrains reader, 64 KiB cap). daemon.json is repository content.

Deliverable:
- One small helper that reads at most 65537 bytes, used by every daemon.json read.
- At each call site, a file over 64 KiB (65536 bytes) is handled like an unparseable one.
- Valid files behave as today.

Not in scope: JetBrains (task-4f1e37f3), connection and retry behaviour, and the other clients, which have their own sibling tasks.

Verification: cd moe-vscode && npm test && npm run compile.
definitionOfDone: Every daemon.json read in MoeDaemonClient.ts and extension.ts goes through one helper that reads at most 65537 bytes; a grep finds no other readFileSync of daemon.json in moe-vscode/src.
A node:test case proves the helper accepts a valid 65536-byte daemon.json, treats a 65537-byte one as unreadable, and refuses a sparse multi-GiB file promptly.
Fresh cd moe-vscode && npm test && npm run compile exits 0.
